editorial:
Shivering Shakespeare is the 95th Our Gang comedy and the final short directed by Robert A. McGowan, who worked under the pseudonym Anthony Mack to distinguish himself from his uncle, the series' senior producer. Released January 25, 1930, the twenty-minute talkie follows the gang as they stage 'The Gladiator's Dilemma,' a school play so badly written and performed that it collapses into a full-scale pie fight. Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer registered the copyright as LP920 on December 17, 1929, and renewed it as R182608 on December 19, 1956 â€” filing within the 28th year of a 1929 copyright, which is valid. Under the Sonny Bono Copyright Term Extension Act's 95-year term, that protection expired December 31, 2024. The print, the original dialogue-and-music track, and the screenplay are all in the public domain as of January 1, 2025.

For creators the appeal is a self-contained ensemble comedy with no prior literary source to untangle: Norman Chaney, Jackie Cooper, Allen Hoskins (Farina), Bobby Hutchins (Wheezer), Mary Ann Jackson, and Pete the Pup are all free to use in their 1930 incarnations. The one real trap is the franchise trademark layer. 'Our Gang' (Warner Bros. Discovery) and 'Little Rascals' (CBS Media Ventures / Paramount) are both actively registered marks that copyright expiry does not touch. A documentary or compilation that lifts the footage and uses an original title is clear; one that labels itself 'Our Gang' or 'Little Rascals' in its title or branding needs trademark clearance from two separate rights holders.
faq: Can I sell copies or stream this film commercially without a license?

Yes. Copyright LP920 expired December 31, 2024 â€” no license is needed to copy, distribute, broadcast, or adapt the original film or its soundtrack. Be careful with third-party sources: some circulating compilations add a new introductory narration or score that would carry its own copyright, and that added material is not covered by the 1929 expiry.
Can I title my project 'Our Gang' or 'Little Rascals'?

No without trademark clearance. Both names are active franchise marks held by separate companies â€” Warner Bros. Discovery for 'Our Gang' and CBS Media Ventures / Paramount for 'Little Rascals.' Trademark rights do not expire with copyright. Choose a descriptive or original title for any derivative work and you avoid the issue entirely.
